scope: Stored abstract of the review of anti-GBM disease: lung and kidney capillaries, RPGN, alveolar haemorrhage, and treatment with steroids, cyclophosphamide, and plasmapheresis.

keyRecommendations.text: Anti-GBM disease is a rare small-vessel vasculitis of kidney and lung capillaries. Most patients develop rapidly progressive crescentic glomerulonephritis, and 40–60% have alveolar haemorrhage.
Initial therapy is corticosteroids and cyclophosphamide to reduce antibody production, and plasmapheresis to remove circulating antibody.
Dialysis at presentation or a high proportion of crescents predicts poor renal outcome. Relapse is rare; renal disease should raise suspicion of concomitant ANCA disease.

clinicalBottomLine: Treat anti-GBM disease urgently with corticosteroids, cyclophosphamide, and plasmapheresis. Expect poor renal recovery if the patient already needs dialysis or the biopsy is crescent-rich.
notableCaveats: The stored text is the abstract, not the full article. Doses are not stated and are not invented here.

source.title: Goodpasture syndrome and anti-glomerular basement membrane disease.
